items.title: Necessary
items.pass_criterion: The obligation answers a real allocated need, applicable interface constraint, or justified derived need from the next higher level; its purpose is identifiable.
items.typical_defect: Speculative feature or needless implementation preference.

items.title: Correct / source-faithful
items.pass_criterion: Behaviour, conditions, terminology and constraints agree with approved input evidence (allocated needs, architecture, interface contracts, platform or hardware references); any derivation has an explicit rationale. Values, limits, error codes and safety reactions are never invented; absent or contradictory input is recorded as a gap (NEEDS_INPUT).
items.typical_defect: Changed threshold, or assumed hardware/platform behaviour, without authority in the inputs.

items.title: Unambiguous
items.pass_criterion: A competent author, implementer and verifier reach one intended interpretation; actors, states, signals, conditions and units are defined or precisely referenced.

items.title: Complete within its scope
items.pass_criterion: The statement contains enough trigger/precondition, required response and observable outcome to be understood without guessing; it may reference a controlled definition (glossary, interface specification, mode or parameter table).
items.typical_defect: Unspecified response on a defined trigger.

items.title: Atomic / singular
items.pass_criterion: It contains one independently judgeable obligation. Requirements are split when one behaviour could pass while another fails.
items.typical_defect: One statement combining initialisation, diagnostics and recovery.

items.title: Objectively verifiable
items.pass_criterion: A verifier can decide pass/fail by test, analysis, inspection or demonstration using stated conditions and observable criteria. Values and tolerances are explicit where needed and source-justified, not manufactured to look measurable.

items.title: Technically feasible
items.pass_criterion: No identified platform, resource, timing, safety or interface constraint makes the requirement impossible; any uncertainty is recorded for analysis.
items.typical_defect: A deadline below what the supported hardware can achieve.

items.title: Design-independent unless justified
items.pass_criterion: Describes required behaviour, not an arbitrary algorithm, hardware access sequence, data structure, partitioning or coding technique. A design constraint is allowed when explicitly allocated and sourced, with the reason recorded.
items.typical_defect: Mandating a lookup table with no upstream justification.

items.title: Consistent
items.pass_criterion: Does not contradict relevant upstream constraints, peer requirements, interface contracts or defined modes.

items.title: Appropriate abstraction level
items.pass_criterion: States the externally relevant obligations, constraints and interfaces of its own level (system or software); leaves unnecessary decomposition to the architecture and design stages below.
items.typical_defect: Implementation pseudocode or element-internal detail presented as a requirement.

items.title: Clear and conforming
items.pass_criterion: Uses controlled vocabulary, consistent naming and units, exactly one mandatory verb (typically "shall") and the project's approved writing pattern (e.g. an EARS-style template). The single-"shall" check is syntactic only; it does not prove atomicity, correctness or testability.
items.typical_defect: Vague pronouns, mixed units, no stated subject, or two "shall" clauses.

items.title: Identifiable and attributable
items.pass_criterion: Has a stable unique ID and source or derivation references; required project metadata (e.g. type, status, verification method) is available without bloating the statement.
items.typical_defect: Unnumbered text with no provenance or change identity.
